propositions: Git probes in repo-isolation guards (porcelain and head) lack subprocess timeout and can block indefinitely, keeping pytest alive after tests complete.
The autouse _no_repo_commits fixture and pytest_sessionfinish hook both invoke unbounded read-only Git probes that should fail fast and explicitly on timeout rather than silently returning None.
Test monkeypatches of subprocess.run and time.sleep can contaminate the repo-isolation guard if the guard dereferences mutable module attributes instead of binding the real runner at import time.
The fixed 5-second watchdog for Git probes must be implemented with explicit subprocess.TimeoutExpired re-raise while preserving None for ordinary OSError and non-repository failures.
Both head() and porcelain() probes must route through a module-scoped bound subprocess.run reference and stable time.sleep namespace to prevent test-double contamination of the safety guard.
